title: Non-overlapping Intervals
keyIdea: Minimum removals = n − (most intervals you can keep without overlap). Keeping as many as possible is activity selection: sort by end and always keep the interval that ends first, since it leaves the most room. Anything starting before the last kept end overlaps and is removed.

approaches.name: Greedy by earliest end
approaches.idea: Your code: sort by end, prevEnd = first end; each interval with start < prevEnd is removed (count++), otherwise kept (prevEnd = its end).
approaches.why: The sort dominates; one pass after it.

quiz.q: Why sort by end and not by start?
options: Ending earliest leaves the most room; by start a long [1,100] could block everything
No; touching is fine, because 2 < 2 is false

quiz.q: When an interval overlaps the last kept one, why remove the new one?
options: Sorted by end, it ends at or after the kept one, so keeping it leaves less room
It came later in the input
